::: {.doc-subject}

An edge ID that doesn't exist in the graph.
:::

::: {.doc-usage-source}
Usage

[Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/errors.py#L35-L56){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
:::

::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS}
```python
EdgeNotFoundError()
```
:::

::: {.doc-text}

Raised whenever a method is given an edge ID that isn't in the graph. Like
`NodeNotFoundError`, it is both a `ValueError` and a `KeyError`.
:::

## Examples {.doc-examples}

::: {#df810e86 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import edgecase as ec

graph = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B"]).add_edge("A", "B")

try:
    graph.get_edge(99)
except ec.EdgeNotFoundError as e:
    print(e)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Edge with ID 99 does not exist
```
:::
:::
